# Supermatter Stability
The Supermatter continuously monitors its own structural stability.
When stability falls below safe operating levels, the crystal automatically broadcasts warnings to the station's engineering radio network.
Stability is influenced by the environment surrounding the crystal. Engineers should continuously monitor chamber conditions and respond to any unexpected changes.
## Sources of Stress
The Supermatter becomes less stable whenever additional energy is introduced into the crystal.
Common sources include:
- High temperatures, above 350 K - Overpressure, above 300 kPa - Low pressure, below 50 kPa - Emitter shots - Laser impacts - Physical contact with the crystal
As stress increases, the crystal becomes more difficult to control.
## Chamber Conditions
The atmosphere surrounding the crystal plays a major role in maintaining stability.
Engineers should monitor:
- Temperature - Pressure - Atmospheric composition
Standard station atmospheric conditions have proven to be a reliable operating environment.
Significant changes should only be performed after careful planning.
## Improving Stability
Proper chamber design improves the crystal's tolerance to changing operating conditions.
Cooling systems connected directly to the chamber should include overpressure countermeasures.
Pressure regulators can be connected to the cooling loop and chamber to prevent excessive pressure buildup.
Additional inlet valves provide further protection against overpressure events by allowing pressure to be controlled at multiple points within the system.
Higher-capacity cooling systems may also be installed.
Hellfire Freezers provide increased cooling capacity, allowing the system to remove heat more effectively and maintain the chamber closer to the desired temperature setpoint during high-stress operation.
